text.p: Motorola Inc's Information Systems Group said Monday it plans to introduce modems allowing data connections up to 56 kilobits per second -- 70 percent faster than today's fastest modems.
In addtion Motorola said it is spearheading an industry effort to standardize new high-speed modem technologies.
Motorola intends to develop and introduce its own modems based on the impending standard in 1997.
The company said the new 56,000 bit modems would be part of its broader line of ISDN, cable modem and other high-speed communications products.
The current standard for consumer modems is V.34, which allows for data transmission at 28.8 kilobits, or thousands of bits, per second.
Motorola said other vendors are expected to indicate their intent to support the standards effort later this month.

Motorola said it will play a major role in facilitating the standards discussion and interaction with the International Telecommunications Union (ITU), the international standards body, for eventual ratification and adoption worldwide.

As it has with virtually all earlier modem standards, Motorola said it is working with other leaders in the data communications industry to define the technology components of the yet-to-be-named new modem standard to ensure compatibility and interoperability between different manufacturers.
Web-surfing, telecommuting, mobile computing and multimedia applications are driving the need for increased data speeds, Motorola said.
Motorola said it has had 56 Kbps modem technology in development for some time.
As part of its international development effort, Motorola is working with Institut Eurecom, an engineering school and research center located in Sophia Antipolis, France.
In addition, Motorola said it has been working in partnership with Institut Eurecom on mixed ISDN-modem systems.
